vasant-shinde-archaeologist.name: Vasant Shinde
vasant-shinde-archaeologist.summary: Indian archaeologist who excavated Rakhigarhi from 2011 to 2016 and led a 2019 genetic study of a Harappan skeleton, though he later publicly endorsed the rival Out of India theory.

bindeshwari-prasad-sinha.name: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
bindeshwari-prasad-sinha.summary: An Indian archaeologist and historian (1919–2002) who led the first excavations at the ancient Buddhist site of Vikramashila and founded Bihar's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

ur.name: Ur
ur.summary: A major Sumerian city-state in ancient Mesopotamia dating from about 3800 BC, whose patron deity was the moon god Nanna and whose ziggurat still stands partially restored.

akkadian-empire.name: Akkadian Empire
akkadian-empire.summary: An ancient kingdom established around 2300 BCE, often considered the first empire in world history, uniting Akkadian and Sumerian speakers across Mesopotamia under Sargon of Akkad and his successors.

meluhha.name: Meluhha
meluhha.summary: The Sumerian name for a major Bronze Age trading partner of Sumer, generally identified by scholars with the Indus Valley Civilisation.

mohenjo-daro.name: Mohenjo-daro
mohenjo-daro.summary: One of the largest cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, built around 2500 BCE and home to at least 40,000 people before being abandoned by about 1700 BCE.

harappa.name: Harappa
harappa.summary: Ancient city in Punjab, Pakistan, that gave its name to the Indus Valley Civilisation's Mature Harappan phase (2600–1900 BC), with up to 23,500 residents at its height.

lothal.name: Lothal
lothal.summary: A southern outpost of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation in Gujarat, India, whose construction began around 2300 BCE.

dholavira.name: Dholavira
dholavira.summary: An archaeological site in Gujarat, India, containing ruins of a city of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, repeatedly damaged by earthquakes, including a severe one around 2600 BCE.

daimabad.name: Daimabad
daimabad.summary: An archaeological site in Maharashtra, India, where excavations uncovered a hoard of bronze figures influenced by Harappan culture, controversially dated to around 1500 BCE.

balathal.name: Balathal
balathal.summary: An archaeological site in Udaipur district, Rajasthan, India, one of ninety sites of the Ahar-Banas culture along the Banas river basin.

ahar-banas-culture.name: Ahar–Banas culture
ahar-banas-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic culture along Rajasthan's Ahar and Banas rivers, lasting from about 3000 to 1500 BCE and contemporary with the Indus Valley civilization, whose people mined Aravalli copper for tools.

copper-hoard-culture.name: Copper Hoard culture
copper-hoard-culture.summary: Term for large and small hoards of copper artefacts found mainly in northern India, dated to the first half of the 2nd millennium BCE and linked to Ochre Coloured Pottery.

cemetery-h-culture.name: Cemetery H culture
cemetery-h-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture of the northern Indian subcontinent from about 1900 to 1300 BCE, seen as a late regional phase of the Harappan civilisation and linked to Indo-Aryan migrations.

madho-sarup-vats.name: Madho Sarup Vats
madho-sarup-vats.summary: Indian archaeologist (1896-1955) who led the Archaeological Survey of India and supervised the excavations at Mohenjodaro from 1924.

black-and-red-ware.name: Black and Red ware
black-and-red-ware.summary: A South Asian pottery style found from the Neolithic through the Iron Age, made by several different cultures rather than one; in parts of India it dates from about 1450 to 700–500 BCE.

sinauli.name: Sinauli
sinauli.summary: Archaeological site in Uttar Pradesh, India, where Bronze Age burials (c. 2000–1500 BCE) yielded wooden carts with solid disk wheels, some argued to be early chariots.

ochre-coloured-pottery-culture.name: Ochre Coloured Pottery culture
ochre-coloured-pottery-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture of the Indo-Gangetic Plain, generally dated 2000–1500 BCE, showing links to both the Late Harappan and Vedic cultures.

battle-of-the-ten-kings.name: Battle of the Ten Kings
battle-of-the-ten-kings.summary: A battle described in the Rigveda in which the Bharata king Sudas defeated a confederation of ten rival tribes, leading to the Kuru polity and possibly inspiring the later Mahabharata's Kurukshetra War.

ravi-river.name: Ravi River (Parushni)
ravi-river.summary: A river flowing through northwestern India and eastern Pakistan, forming part of the border between the two countries and one of the five major rivers of the Punjab region.

bharatas-vedic-tribe.name: Bharatas
bharatas-vedic-tribe.summary: An early Vedic tribe from the second millennium BCE whose king Sudās won the Battle of the Ten Kings, after which its people helped form the Kuru kingdom, India's first attested state.

sudas.name: Sudas
sudas.summary: Indo-Aryan tribal king of the Bharatas (c. 14th century BCE) who won the Battle of the Ten Kings, establishing Bharata dominance and paving the way for the later Kuru tribal union.

michael-witzel.name: Michael Witzel
michael-witzel.summary: German-American philologist and Indologist, a former Harvard professor of Sanskrit who has researched Indian sacred texts, especially the Vedas.

divodasa.name: Divodasa
divodasa.summary: Indo-Aryan king of the Bharata tribe during the Rigvedic period, celebrated in the Rigveda for defeating the chieftain Sambara and father of the later king Sudas.

doab.name: Doab
doab.summary: A South Asian term, from Persian for 'two waters', for the tract of land lying between two confluent rivers.

d-p-agrawal.name: D. P. Agrawal
d-p-agrawal.summary: A historian of Indian science and technology, archaeologist and author who has written on Indian archaeology, metallurgy, and palaeoclimate.

ashvamedha.name: Ashvamedha
ashvamedha.summary: A Vedic horse-sacrifice ritual in which a king's horse wandered freely for a year; if no rival captured it, the king was declared undisputed sovereign and the horse was sacrificed.

khandava-forest.name: Khandava Forest
khandava-forest.summary: A forest west of the Yamuna river in the epic Mahabharata, inhabited by Naga serpent-people before it was burned to build the Pandavas' capital, Indraprastha.

vajra.name: Vajra
vajra.summary: A ritual thunderbolt-shaped tool used in Hindu, Buddhist and Jain traditions to symbolize indestructibility and spiritual power, also linked to the Vedic god Indra.

indra.name: Indra
indra.summary: The Vedic god of weather, storms and war, regarded as king of the gods in early Hinduism and the most frequently mentioned deity in the Rigveda, celebrated for slaying the demon Vritra.

paul-alan-yule.name: Paul Alan Yule
paul-alan-yule.summary: German archaeologist at Heidelberg University whose work focuses on the archaeology of Oman and Yemen, and previously India.

rigveda.name: Rigveda
rigveda.summary: An ancient collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns, the oldest known Vedic text and one of the four sacred Hindu Vedas, most likely composed between about 1500 and 1000 BCE in northwestern India.

historical-vedic-religion.name: Historical Vedic religion
historical-vedic-religion.summary: The religious ideas and practices of Indo-Aryan peoples in northwest India during the Vedic period (c. 1500–500 BCE), recorded in Vedic texts and one of the major traditions that shaped modern Hinduism.

indus-script.name: Indus script
indus-script.summary: A still-undeciphered set of symbols used by the Indus Valley Civilisation, known from thousands of very short inscriptions with no bilingual text to aid translation.

girnar.name: Girnar
girnar.summary: An ancient hill near Junagadh, Gujarat, sacred to Jains as the place where the 22nd Tirthankar attained enlightenment and nirvana.

lahuradewa.name: Lahuradewa
lahuradewa.summary: An archaeological site in Uttar Pradesh, India, noted for early pottery and among the earliest evidence of rice cultivation, occupied from as early as 9000 BCE.

rakesh-tewari.name: Rakesh Tewari
rakesh-tewari.summary: Indian archaeologist (born 1953) who led the Archaeological Survey of India from 2014 to 2017 and showed that rice was cultivated in the subcontinent as early as the 9th millennium BP.

tuyere.name: Tuyere
tuyere.summary: A tube or pipe used to blow air into a furnace or hearth so a fire becomes hot enough to smelt or forge metal, in use since the Iron Age.

sivagalai.name: Sivagalai
sivagalai.summary: A village in the Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu, India, surrounded by small hamlets and about 30 km from Tuticorin city.

atharvaveda.name: Atharvaveda
atharvaveda.summary: The fourth Veda of Hinduism, a collection of about 730 hymns covering everyday rituals, initiation, marriage and funerals alongside its more magical formulas.

sushruta-samhita.name: Sushruta Samhita
sushruta-samhita.summary: Ancient Sanskrit medical text and a foundational work of Ayurveda, notable for uniquely detailed chapters on surgical training, instruments, and procedures; its oldest surviving manuscript dates to 878 CE.

fatehgarh.name: Fatehgarh
fatehgarh.summary: A cantonment town on the south bank of the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, India, named after an old fort and now home to a major Indian Army training establishment.

myaladumparai.name: Myaladumparai
myaladumparai.summary: A village in Theni district, Tamil Nadu, India, with a population of 29,731 as of 2011.

kikata.name: Kikata
kikata.summary: An ancient Indian kingdom mentioned in the Vedas, described in the Rigveda as a non-Vedic people who did not perform Vedic rituals; its exact location is debated.

kurukshetra.name: Kurukshetra
kurukshetra.summary: A historical region in India also known as the 'Land of the Bhagavad Gita,' and the city that is now headquarters of Kurukshetra district in Haryana.

magadha.name: Magadha
magadha.summary: Ancient Indian kingdom in the eastern Ganges Plain that formed the core of major dynasties including the Mauryan and Gupta empires, and played a key role in the development of Buddhism and Jainism.

chedi-kingdom.name: Chedi kingdom
chedi-kingdom.summary: An ancient Indian kingdom located in the Bundelkhand region of present-day Madhya Pradesh, with its capital city called Suktimati.

vedic-period.name: Vedic period
vedic-period.summary: A period in India's late Bronze and early Iron Age, roughly 1500 to 500 BCE, when the Vedas were composed by Indo-Aryan tribes who had migrated into the northwestern subcontinent.

agama-hinduism.name: Agamas
agama-hinduism.summary: A body of Tantric Hindu scriptures in Sanskrit and Tamil covering cosmology, meditation, and temple worship, in existence by around the mid-1st millennium CE.

indo-gangetic-plain.name: Indo-Gangetic Plain
indo-gangetic-plain.summary: A fertile plain of about 700,000 square kilometers across northern South Asia, named for the Indus and Ganges rivers whose silt built its vast alluvial soil.

painted-grey-ware-culture.name: Painted Grey Ware culture
painted-grey-ware-culture.summary: An Iron Age culture of the western Gangetic plain and Ghaggar-Hakra valley in India, dated roughly 1200 to 500 BCE, known for fine painted grey pottery and early towns.

iravatham-mahadevan.name: Iravatham Mahadevan
iravatham-mahadevan.summary: Indian epigraphist and civil servant (1930-2018), known for deciphering Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions and for his expertise on the epigraphy of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

jonathan-mark-kenoyer.name: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
jonathan-mark-kenoyer.summary: American archaeologist (born 1952) and professor of anthropology focused on the Indus Valley Civilization and its trade links to surrounding regions.

kenneth-a-r-kennedy.name: Kenneth A. R. Kennedy
kenneth-a-r-kennedy.summary: American anthropologist (1930–2014) at Cornell University specializing in forensic anthropology and human skeletal biology.

j-p-mallory.name: J. P. Mallory
j-p-mallory.summary: American archaeologist and Indo-Europeanist, born 1945, emeritus professor at Queen's University Belfast.

douglas-q-adams.name: Douglas Q. Adams
douglas-q-adams.summary: American linguist and Indo-European specialist, an expert on the Tocharian languages, who has co-authored works on Indo-European culture with J. P. Mallory.

asko-parpola.name: Asko Parpola
asko-parpola.summary: Finnish Indologist, born 1941, Professor Emeritus at the University of Helsinki, specializing in the Indus Valley Civilization and its undeciphered script.

saharanpur-district.name: Saharanpur district
saharanpur-district.summary: The northernmost district of India's Uttar Pradesh state, bordering Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand near the Shivalik Hills, with headquarters in the city of Saharanpur.

yama.name: Yama
yama.summary: Hindu god of death and justice who judges the souls of the dead; Vedic tradition holds he was the first mortal to die and find the way to the afterlife.
